raw_response:
I farm the same 5 mu in the wheat-maize cycle, same as I have done for years. I do not start from empty. I start from what worked before and look at the sky, the water, and what the neighbors are doing. On my land, if I go short on fertilizer, the crop shows it fast, and once yield is lost I cannot get it back. So I will not be stingy with the base fertilizer. I have well water, so I will use that to steady the crop when it turns dry. For wheat, I will keep all 5 mu in winter wheat, use improved seed like most people around here do now, put more nitrogen than phosphorus, and add some potassium so the straw stays stronger. I will water around the wintering stage, jointing stage, and grain filling if the field is dry. For maize after wheat, I will sow all 5 mu again, use hybrid seed, and feed it a bit heavier because maize eats fertilizer and if ears are small, that hurts badly. I will still watch costs, because I only have 5 mu and every bag costs money, but I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose harvest. I will do rotary tillage after each crop because it is faster and cheaper for my small area than deep ploughing every time. For pests, I will spray when I usually do, not too many times, just enough to keep worms and disease from taking the crop.
